Lemma
[No sub-geodesic of Dx is an embedded loop in A] No sub-geodesic of any $D_x$ is an embedded loop in $A$.
Proof

↗ lem:no-geodesic-spans-c0-to-c0 \sketch The null-homotopic case is Lemma 6. For an essential loop, compactify the complementary component containing $c_0\setminus \{ x\} $ as a disk and repeat the maximal-focusing argument. At least $0.86$ length of final radial endpoints cannot lie on the loop segment of length below $0.2$, so some radial joins two points of $c_0$, contradicting Lemma 6.

□
